suggestions.assertion: Generated proposal header blockquote contains a line starting exactly with `> **Linked Issue**:` (canonical English spelling; `关联 Issue` alias, `Related Issue`, or omitting the line fails)
suggestions.reason: Passed in BOTH arms. The old_skill (baseline) arm also emitted the canonical `> **Linked Issue**: \`none\`` line, so this assertion cannot attribute the behavior to the skill diff. Root cause visible in the sibling eval: old_skill eval-3 answer.md:9 says it followed 'standards/openspec/templates/proposal-minimal.md 的 Usage Notes'. The shared SOT template already carries the field, so the new behavior leaks into the baseline arm through the repo, not through the skill. For a discriminating AB the baseline must be isolated from the template change (pin the template to its pre-change SHA in the old_skill arm, or assert something only the skill instruction can produce).

suggestions.assertion: Since the prompt names no tracking issue, the Linked Issue value is exactly `none` inside an inline code span (a left-in placeholder such as `{<org>/<repo>#<n>}`, an empty value, `N/A`, or a markdown link fails)
suggestions.reason: Passed in BOTH arms (non-discriminating). Also a wording gap: 'exactly `none`' is enforced by the extractor as 'first inline-code token == none', and it accepts trailing prose after the code span (old_skill proposal.md:6 is `\`none\` — verified 2026-09-02: Forgejo issue search ...`). The fail-list (placeholder / empty / N/A / link) is enumerative and does not say whether annotation on the field line is allowed. Decide and encode it; a downstream consumer that expects a bare sentinel would treat these two arms differently while the grader treats them the same.

suggestions.assertion: Should correctly parse mixed Chinese/English input
suggestions.reason: Passed in BOTH arms and near-trivial: the two halves of the input are exact synonyms, so any dark-mode proposal written in English 'parses' it. A discriminating bilingual eval gives complementary information per language (e.g. English states the feature, Chinese states a constraint or target module) and asserts both facts survive into the proposal.

suggestions.assertion: Should preserve the feature intent from both language inputs
suggestions.reason: Passed in BOTH arms; same triviality as assertion 1 (there is no divergent intent to preserve). Note the observed re-scoping: both arms turned 'add a dark mode feature' into 'add a system/dark/light theme mode with light palette + toggle + persistence' because the dashboard is already dark-only. Whether that is the desired interpretation or scope creep is an important outcome no assertion covers.

suggestions.assertion: Should generate proposal content in English as requested
suggestions.reason: Passed in BOTH arms. Both proposals contain short quoted Chinese fragments (with_skill :43 `CLAUDE.md "向后兼容"`, :96 `宁跑勿豁`; old_skill :8 verbatim source request, :9 quoted precedent, :15 quoted issue title). The assertion should state whether quotation of Chinese SOT/source text is acceptable; otherwise the verdict rests on grader judgment.
No assertion checks Level 2 shape (proposal.md only, no tasks.md), header order, or that the executor did not write into the repository — all observed outcomes with no coverage.

eval_feedback.overall: 5/5 passed in both arms; zero discriminating assertions. The two linked-issue assertions (the iteration-1 target) pass in the baseline because the shared standards template already supplies the canonical field — the AB design leaks the new behavior into old_skill.
